question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the post-stimulus window
ideas.description: Use dTAG or auxin-inducible degradation of Fos or Jun after an initial stimulus, then re-stimulate. If the second response and chromatin priming fail when AP-1 is removed during washout, AP-1 is necessary for memory maintenance rather than only for initial induction.

ideas.title: Pulse-interval series to measure memory decay kinetics
ideas.description: Deliver two stimulus pulses separated by systematically varied intervals, using optogenetic or precisely timed ligand pulses, and measure the second response (transcription, AP-1 binding, accessibility). The interval-dependence curve gives a quantitative memory timescale that can be compared against models of simple signal carryover.

ideas.title: Motif-level editing of AP-1 sites at memory enhancers
ideas.description: Use base editing or CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs at enhancers that gain accessibility or activity after stimulation, leaving neighboring sequence intact. Measuring whether the motif loss abolishes priming and faster re-induction tests whether the AP-1 site itself, rather than the bound factor or general chromatin state, encodes memory.

ideas.title: Mitotic inheritance of AP-1-primed chromatin
ideas.description: Synchronize cells, stimulate, and track AP-1 occupancy and accessibility through mitosis into daughter cells, combining mitotic ChIP or CUT&Tag with clonal readouts. Retention of the primed state across division would indicate heritable memory, whereas loss would indicate that memory depends on continuous AP-1 presence.

ideas.title: Barcoded single-cell lineage tracing of memory heterogeneity
ideas.description: Introduce lineage barcodes and a fluorescent AP-1 target reporter, then stimulate cells and follow clonal lineages over several divisions. Comparing memory between sister and unrelated clones reveals whether memory is cell-autonomous, inherited, and bistable or whether it is a graded, population-level effect.

candidates: Time-course CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag of AP-1 occupancy at enhancers after stimulus washout
Acute degradation (dTAG/AID) of Fos or Jun during the post-stimulus window to test whether AP-1 is required for memory maintenance
Live single-cell Fos reporter pulse-chase to measure how long the induced state persists
Varying interval between two stimulus pulses to map the decay kinetics of the memory of the first pulse
ATAC-seq persistence of chromatin accessibility at AP-1 motifs after stimulus removal
Tracking H3K27ac and H3K4me1/2 persistence at primed AP-1 enhancers over days to weeks
Long-term tracking of DNA methylation or repressive marks at AP-1 sites as a slower epigenetic memory layer
Base-editing or CRISPR mutation of AP-1 motifs at memory enhancers to test whether the motif itself is required for memory
Synthetic Fos autoregulatory loop to test whether a feedback circuit alone can generate bistable, heritable memory
Lineage-traced clonal analysis to see whether memory of prior stimulation is inherited through cell divisions
Mitotic bookmarking assays: does AP-1 stay bound to chromatin through mitosis and reset accessibility afterward
Single-molecule tracking of Fos/Jun residence time in primed versus naive cells
Phospho-proteomic and protein half-life analysis of AP-1 subunits to test whether protein stability carries memory
Transcript half-life measurements for AP-1 target mRNAs to separate transcript persistence from chromatin memory
Mathematical model fits comparing memory-like persistence against simple signal carryover or ligand retention
Heterologous memory test: does a prior stimulus change the response to an unrelated stimulus through shared AP-1 sites
In vitro reconstitution of AP-1 with nucleosomal arrays under pulsed input to test if memory is encoded in chromatin alone
Ex vivo or in vivo tissue comparisons of activity-dependent AP-1 memory versus cultured cells
Hi-C or Micro-C changes at AP-1 enhancer loops after stimulus, and whether loops persist
Competitive decoy TRE oligos or dominant-negative Jun to test sequence specificity of any memory effect
Transcription inhibitor washout experiments to test whether memory requires ongoing transcription
Endogenous epitope-tagged Jun knock-in for CUT&Tag tracking across divisions and stimulation cycles
